Guidance & outlook: In FY26, we sold more than 3.9 million of this control intensive ECUs, which was more than 60% compared to FY25.
So coming to Q4 FY26 financials, there is a very big revenue growth that we have seen in Q4, more than 60%, along with even higher growth, even higher growth in our profitability.
So our FY26 revenue was 1,058 crore, the first time that we have crossed 1,000 crore in revenue, highest ever.
Growth & demand: And this strong revenue growth has also come with a growth in profitability percentage as well, as well as much higher growth in the absolute terms in profits.
If you look at the FY26 volume growth, more than 80% of that came because of SEDEMAC.
So in terms of volume, ISG volumes are roughly, power tools volume are roughly 4 to 5x of. of ISG volumes.
Margins & costs: Okay, so if you simply look at these numbers, then this year we did 1058 crore with high capacity utilization, which essentially means that Amit Dixit 16:44 this 227 crore of tangible investment that we have done, that has led to roughly, you can say, 1058 crore of revenue.
So our EBIT percentage, if you see our EBITDA has been more than 20% and our EBIT is roughly 15%.

Okay, so to summarize, we have had a very strong FY26, strong revenue growth, 60% plus, and now we are more, we are 1000 crore plus revenue company, more than 200 crore EBITDA, 21% EBITDA percentage, and more than 100 crore PAT with extremely strong RoCE.
Capex & expansion: So some things that are useful to note is that if you look at the plant CapEx, so if you just look at this number, this 227 crore is the cumulative plant CapEx that we have done till March of 2025.
And if the utilisation of capacity is high, then this plant CapEx to this revenue, next year's revenue, because of course the planned CapEx has to be done in a few months ahead.
Okay, so roughly, you would say 20% to 22% sort of Amit Dixit 17:05 CapEx, plant CapEx is required or tangible CapEx is required for us to generate additional revenue compared to what we have today.
Balance sheet & cash: So we have debt, then the internal accruals and the equity capital, these three.
We have had 135 crore of working capital investment, so that gives you a ratio of about 13% or so.
And so plant CapEx and roughly 13 crore to 15 crore or maybe 12 to 15 crore. in working capital.
Risks & challenges: Similarly, if you look at the working capital number, which tends to be more, you know, less of a delay between the investment and the realisation of revenue.
So in the first week of May, we had conducted this survey of risk assessment where we had invited about 20 of the investment professionals to provide feedback on the risks in our business.
This risk is low, you know, that sort of a thing, and then the overall risk score.
